answer: A verifiable delay protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to submit non-parallelizable sequential proofs evaluated by the consensus kernel. To unleash a gale of concurrent identities into the network oasis, an attacker must dedicate scarce high-frequency processor cores and uninterrupted wall-clock time per node. This ties identity scalability to physical execution latency. However, this continuous computation wastes energy and disadvantages low-power edge agents.
